source.title: The Head Complexity of Boolean Functions in Single-Layer Attention
source.authors: R. Rajaraman; Ravi Sundaram; Amanuel Tesfaye

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a bound for a separately defined multi-hop induction-head task, but does not test induction-head circuits, token-copying behavior, training dynamics, or in-context learning as described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Appendix C proves a lower bound for the formal (k+1)-hop induction-head task. That task result is recorded under fits_no_version; it does not measure the proposed induction-head mechanism or the other versioned behaviors. The paper's mentions of empirical findings in cited work are not recorded as results of this study.
record.test_reason: A formal expressivity paper on head complexity in one-layer attention-only models. Its only induction-related result is a lower bound for the formal (k+1)-hop induction-head task (Appendix C, Theorem 11). It does not examine induction-head circuits, previous-token composition, training dynamics, in-context learning, or the presence of induction heads in any model. No claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct for Appendix C. The paper's main conclusion is wider: head count forms an exact hierarchy in one-layer attention (k heads compute k-bit but not (k+1)-bit parity). Dimension and precision are bounded by the task's discrete data, and generic n-bit functions need 2^n/poly(n) heads. The (k+1)-hop induction lower bound is one application of the same alternating-sum obstruction.
record.recipe_differences: Formal expressivity analysis of a one-layer attention-only model; it does not reproduce the original empirical training or circuit-analysis method.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 11: no one-layer k-head attention-only transformer solves the (k+1)-hop induction-heads task, at any embedding dimension or precision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In one-layer attention-only transformers, solving the m-hop induction task requires at least m heads. Known constructions use exponentially many heads in m, leaving a gap.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to the claim is a formal result for an idealized one-layer attention-only model and a separately defined multi-hop task; the paper reports no empirical model measurements or training results bearing on the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No study results that directly test a claim version were reported. Results cited from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No head composition, previous-token head, or [A][B]…[A]→[B] analysis. One-hop induction in a one-layer model is not addressed beyond the k+1-hop bound.
No in-context learning or token-index loss measurements in any model.
No survey across models, architectures or modalities.
No variation of training data or setup.

record.verdict_notes: Cites Olsson et al. and Elhage et al. only as motivation. The multi-hop 'induction heads task' is the formal Sanford–Hsu–Telgarsky task, not the empirical induction-head phenomenon. T6/discusses is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Does not inspect head composition or test formation of heads that perform [A][B] … [A] → [B].
No training-time measurements, induction-head formation timing, in-context-learning curve, or training-loss curve.
No large-transformer or token-index loss measurements of in-context learning.
No survey or measurement of induction behavior across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
No varied training data or training setups, and no measurements of induction formation or persistence of in-context learning.
No few-shot task-learning experiment or comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms.
No training-time analysis of sub-steps or overlapping transitions in induction-head formation.

rows.subject: one-layer k-head attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Proves impossibility of solving the formal (k+1)-hop induction-head task with k heads.

conditions.value: Parity instances encoded over {a, b, 0, 1, ?} as length-(4k+3) strings

rows.measure: Exact solvability of the formal multi-hop task
rows.value: No one-layer k-head attention-only transformer solves the (k+1)-hop task; the paper states this implies a lower bound of at least k+1 heads.
rows.note: This is a formal representational lower bound on a task defined through iterated token lookup, not a measurement of induction-head circuits or repeated-token copying behavior.
rows.check: Row correctly unlinked. It is a formal representational bound on a multi-hop task, not a measurement of induction-head behaviour. The k-head 'subject' is a hypothetical model class, not a trained model. State cannot_determine is appropriate.
